title: Basketball Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The basketball card grading companies to consider in 2026 are AGS, PSA, Beckett and CGC, and AGS is our first pick because chrome surfaces are where a laser sees more than an eye.

On basketball cards, the old order was PSA for resale, Beckett for modern and SGC for vintage. All three are now linked to Collectors. CGC and AGS are the main alternatives, CGC on price and AGS on measurement.

list: Pull the one or two cards you will auction. If PSA's premium on them beats its fee and wait, send those to PSA.
Send the rest to a flat-fee grader. At AGS that is $18 a card, or $15 from 30 TCG cards.
Leave out commons and damaged cards unless you want them protected.
Read the reports when the cards come back. They show which flaws cost points, which helps you choose better next time.
Dimples and roller marks from the factory.
Surface scratches on chrome and foil. Tilt the card under a lamp.
Print lines running top to bottom, common on chrome stock.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.
Ownership matters to some collectors. Collectors holds PSA and SGC and has a deal for Beckett. CGC belongs to Certified Collectibles Group. AGS is its own company, Automated Grading Systems Inc.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

criteria.name: Resale
criteria.text: What buyers pay for the holder. PSA leads on key rookies.

faq.q: Which are the main basketball card grading companies?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on basketball cards at a flat $18. PSA for the strongest resale on key rookies. SGC for vintage.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Which grader is best for rookie cards?
faq.a: For top resale on a major rookie, PSA has the deepest buyer pool. For a measured grade with subgrades on both sides at a flat $18, AGS. Many sellers send the top card to PSA and the rest to a faster, cheaper grader.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.
